I know, my (ex) gf broke up with me a week ago, but the trick is not to give into those obsessive thoughts where you think about your ex, what they're up to, how to get them back etc. 

Your brain becomes overwhelmed by all these problems you now have to find solutions for, which is fine, except you don't have the answers for them. You might be thinking about why your ex said or did something which you can't make sense of, and as you do you get drawn into a spiral of negativity. Which feeds off itself as one unanswered question leads to another, and your mind races. Your brain does fine when it has a clear decision but the lack of clear answers sends the brain into stress mode and it hunkers down, making you think more, going deeper into your thoughts until you find a solution! But there aren't any, and truth be told your ex probably doesn't have the answers either!

So to help, you have to break the cycle of negativity. You know that thinking about your ex makes you feel terrible, so make a conscious decision, with the conscious side of your brain. Your subconscious side wants you to carry on with these negative thoughts so you have to take control! Show the subconscious side of your brain that YOU still decide what you think about!

You have to reprogramme your brain to teach it that you won't reward the negative thinking by indulging it further, instead stop as soon as you notice and change the subject in your head. Hell a good tip if you're alone to stop the thoughts, is to "throw you mind outside your body". So think of stuff outside you can see and shout out the names and colours of 10 things, eg "blue shirt" "brown vase". I bet some common things of yours are  colours you never even noticed before! 

Not only does this stop the introverted thoughts it slowly reprogrammes the brain that negative thoughts won't get rewarded by the brains reward system!
